staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash from this preserved checkout. The saved symbolized trace names `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` at `xinclude.c:1987`, `xmlXIncludeLoadNode` at `xinclude.c:2150`, `xmlXIncludeDoProcess` at `xinclude.c:2449`, `xmlStaticCopyNode` at `tree.c:4360`, `xmlFreeDoc` at `tree.c:1250`, and the final bad-free sink at `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750.

classification.classification_note: The preserved witness reaches recursive XInclude fallback processing with old-namespace markup (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`) and an `href` beginning `#xpointer`. That old namespace enables `ctxt->legacy`, which lets `xmlXIncludeAddNode` preserve the URI fragment for XPointer evaluation. Vulnerable `xmlXIncludeLoadDoc` then accepts a location-style XPointer result (`XPATH_RANGE` or `XPATH_LOCATIONSET`) instead of rejecting it, materializes replacement nodes from that location object, and splices them into the fallback subtree. Outer fallback handling later recopies `fallback->children`; the saved AddressSanitizer stack proves that this copy unwinds through `xmlStaticCopyNode`, `xmlFreeNode`, `xmlFreeDoc`, and finally `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750, where `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` frees a pointer that AddressSanitizer traced to `xmlDictAddString`. The staged evidence does not isolate which precise location subtype/member produced the document-scoped subtree seen in the rollback stack, so the trace stays branch-agnostic across that middle segment.

bug_description.original: Invalid free and uninitialized-value in XInclude processing: while processing XInclude nodes (xmlXIncludeDoProcess in xinclude.c), libxml2's node-copy/free path (xmlStaticCopyNode/xmlFreeNode/xmlFreeNodeList/xmlFreeDoc in tree.c) attempts to free a pointer that was not returned by malloc (free on an interior address of an allocated block), causing heap corruption and crashes. MSAN also reports a use-of-uninitialized-value in the same XInclude/doc node creation path (xmlDictLookup/xmlNewDocNode), leading to undefined behavior and further memory corruption risk.
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a libxml2 `fuzz/xml` container whose first four bytes decode to the little-endian option word `0x78232467`, which includes `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE`. Its extracted XML strings contain old-namespace XInclude markup (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`), nested `xi:fallback` content, and at least one `xi:include` whose `href` begins with `#xpointer`. On the witnessed path, an include load fails, `xmlXIncludeLoadNode` selects a fallback child, and `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` recursively reprocesses that fallback subtree. In the nested pass, old-namespace markup sets `ctxt->legacy = 1`, `xmlXIncludeAddNode` preserves the `href` fragment as `ref->fragment`, `xmlXIncludeLoadDoc` evaluates it with `xmlXPtrEval`, and vulnerable code admits a location-style result (`XPATH_RANGE` or `XPATH_LOCATIONSET`) instead of rejecting it. XInclude stores the copied location result as the include replacement and splices that replacement into the fallback subtree. Outer fallback handling later calls `xmlDocCopyNodeList(ctxt->doc, fallback->children)`; the saved AddressSanitizer trace shows that copy failing and rolling back through `xmlStaticCopyNode`, `xmlFreeNode`, `xmlFreeDoc`, and finally `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750. AddressSanitizer reports that the freed pointer lies 87 bytes inside a region allocated by `xmlDictAddString` during parse-time dictionary insertion, so when `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` runs in that rollback subtree, the active cleanup scope does not own the retained name pointer. The preserved source and saved artifacts do not prove which exact location-object subtype/member produced the document-node cleanup frame, so this Stage 02 narrative does not claim a narrower middle mechanism.

source.description: First project-side statement on the crashing path that converts attacker-controlled markup into vulnerability-relevant state. During recursive fallback reprocessing, old-namespace XInclude markup sets legacy mode, which later makes the `href` URI fragment admissible as the include fragment.
source.value_from: The preserved `poc` strings show repeated `http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude` and `#xpointer`-prefixed include targets inside fallback content. This assignment is the first project statement on the witnessed path that turns that input into state used by the vulnerable XPointer branch.

root_cause.description: Root cause supported by the staged patch. Vulnerable XInclude processing accepts location-style XPointer objects and continues into the node-copy path instead of rejecting them.
root_cause.note: The staged fix gates location-object support behind `LIBXML_XPTR_LOCS_ENABLED` and disables it by default, removing these `XPATH_RANGE` / `XPATH_LOCATIONSET` branches from the default XInclude path. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build.

sink.description: Crash sink. During rollback of a failed subtree copy, `xmlFreeNodeList` frees a node `name` pointer that actually points inside a dictionary string-pool allocation, matching the saved AddressSanitizer bad-free report.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser gate for the staged witness's main XML entity. The malformed fuzz-container payload still has to present a document body beginning with `<` so libxml2 enters tree parsing and builds the XInclude nodes later processed by `xmlXIncludeTestNode` and `xmlXIncludeAddNode`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment preserves the attacker-controlled XPointer fragment in the XInclude reference record so the later load phase can evaluate it.

coarse_trace.summary: An include load fails, `xmlXIncludeLoadNode` selects a `xi:fallback` child, and fallback handling recursively reprocesses that fallback subtree.
In the nested fallback pass, old-namespace XInclude markup enables legacy mode and allows the attacker-controlled `href` fragment to be stored as the include fragment.
The nested include evaluates that fragment as an XPointer, vulnerable code accepts a location-style result, materializes replacement nodes from it, and splices those nodes into the fallback subtree.

Outer fallback handling recopies the mutated fallback subtree; the copy rolls back and ultimately frees a dictionary string pointer at `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750, matching the saved AddressSanitizer bad-free.

fine_trace.note: The witnessed path reaches fallback handling because an include load failed and `xmlXIncludeLoadNode` found a `xi:fallback` child to process.
Fallback handling explicitly re-enters XInclude processing on the fallback subtree. The next steps occur in this nested `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(..., fallback, 1)` pass.
Source. In the nested fallback pass, the attacker-controlled include node uses `XINCLUDE_OLD_NS`, so XInclude enables legacy mode for this context.
The nested include setup reads the attacker-controlled include target from the parsed `xi:include` element. In the preserved witness this target begins with `#xpointer`.
Because legacy mode is already enabled, `xmlXIncludeAddNode` does not reject the URI fragment. It reuses `uri->fragment` as the include fragment that will drive XPointer evaluation.
The nested include record stores the attacker-controlled fragment for the later load phase.
The load phase evaluates the stored fragment as an XPointer expression and materializes the result in `xptr`.
Root cause. Vulnerable XInclude processing explicitly admits location-style XPointer results instead of rejecting them like the scalar cases above.
The admitted location-style object is handed to the location-copy machinery, and the resulting replacement list is stored for later insertion into the fallback subtree.

The nested include replacement phase splices the location-derived replacement nodes into the fallback subtree, so outer fallback handling will later traverse and recopy them through `fallback->children`.

After the nested pass returns, outer fallback handling recopies the now-mutated fallback children into the outer include replacement list. This exact call is present in the saved AddressSanitizer stack.

depends_on.via: fallback->children now includes nested replacement nodes

fine_trace.note: While outer fallback copying duplicates non-text nodes into `ctxt->doc`, copied names are taken from the target document dictionary through `xmlDictLookup`. The saved AddressSanitizer allocation context shows that the eventually freed pointer came from `xmlDictAddString` in that dictionary machinery during parse-time name interning.

A child copy fails while outer fallback copying is duplicating the fallback subtree, so `xmlStaticCopyNode` rolls back the partially built copy by freeing `ret`. This rollback point is the frame immediately above `xmlFreeNode` in the saved stack.

Rollback cleanup walks the partial copy depth-first. The saved stack proves that a copied document node is present in the failing subtree, so cleanup enters `xmlFreeDoc`. The staged evidence does not isolate which specific location-object subtype/member produced that document node.
`xmlFreeDoc` immediately recurses into the copied document node's child list, establishing the document-scoped cleanup frame directly below the sink in the saved stack.

Sink. `DICT_FREE` calls `xmlFree` when the current-scope dictionary is absent or does not own `cur->name`. AddressSanitizer shows that the pointer freed here is 87 bytes inside an `xmlDictAddString` allocation, so the active cleanup scope at this point is not the owner of the retained dictionary string pointer.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with this trace because it gates the `XPATH_RANGE` / `XPATH_LOCATIONSET` branches behind `LIBXML_XPTR_LOCS_ENABLED` and disables that feature by default, removing the location-object path that feeds the recorded bad-free. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build, so no dynamic fixed-side claim is made here.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged source, patch.diff, and the preserved `poc`

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` and saved the symbolized stack ending at `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3750 during XInclude fallback processing.

format.name: libxml2 `fuzz/xml` container
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged witness at `gt_results/secbench_oss_libxml2.ossfuzz-42510687/poc`. Its load-bearing structure is: a four-byte little-endian option word `0x78232467` with `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` set; then fuzz-container string records whose main XML entity contains old-namespace XInclude markup (`http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude`), fallback content, and at least one `xi:include` whose `href` begins `#xpointer`. This Stage 02 trace is grounded only for that preserved witness shape and does not generalize beyond it.
